label: v4.0.0.11 changes 108 lines of extract-from-evidence.cjs and 69 lines of its vitest but its note never mentions the resource map: rg -c -i 'resource.?map|trigger.?index|retrieval|fixture' returns 0 and the file carries only two headings, 'What's New at a Glance' (line 19) and 'Upgrade' (line 30). The change is not cosmetic: normalizePathCandidate now strips a #anchor before the line suffix, decideStatus routes every citation through a packet root instead of REPO_ROOT, and two new functions findGitWorkTree and resolveExistingDirectory land in the same file, so the release alters how MISSING is decided for every review and research resource map while the note describes none of it.

The trigger corpus indexes this run's own research output, so a research iteration stales the index Gate 1 reads: the manifest excludes **/scratch/**, **/research/lineages/** and specs/**/lineages/** but not specs/**/research/**, and the manifest body lists research artifacts among its included paths. corpusHash therefore moves at every tag (f4851a38 at v4.0.0.10, ea4d23dd at v4.0.0.11, e626e926 at v4.0.0.12, fd0010dd at v4.0.2.0) even though v4.0.0.12 touches no source file at all - its whole four-file delta is trigger-index.json plus the three generator outputs. This is the causal root of the 43-row stale report: the research packet's own spec, tasks, timeline and decision-record are newly added documents, so no amount of rebuilding during a run can leave the index fresh while the run is writing.
verify: rg -n 'research|lineages' .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/fixtures/corpus-manifest.json | head -4; for t in v4.0.0.10 v4.0.0.11 v4.0.0.12; do git show $t:.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/fixtures/corpus-manifest.json | rg -m1 -o '"corpusHash": "[a-f0-9]{16}'; done; git diff --stat v4.0.0.11..v4.0.0.12 -- .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit

label: The same v4.0.0.11 commit adds the citation-anchor strip twice. normalizePathCandidate filters a candidate with /#.*$/ and /:\d+(?:-\d+)?$/ after rejecting ../ traversal, while a new stripCitationSuffix reads indexOf('#') and applies the same line regex with no traversal check at all; determineStatus calls only the second one. One rule, two implementations, differing on whether ./ and ../ are stripped, in a 600-line file. Nothing breaks if determineStatus reuses normalizePathCandidate instead: every caller already passes it a normalized entry, so the second function only restates the first.
verify: rg -n 'stripCitationSuffix|function normalizePathCandidate' .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/resource-map/extract-from-evidence.cjs; git diff v4.0.0.10..v4.0.0.11 -- .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/resource-map/extract-from-evidence.cjs | rg -n '^\+.*replace\(/#|^\+function strip'

label: The .opencode to .skilled move (330427cf30, 2026-09-17) is an attribution wall: plain git log over the current path returns 1 commit for gate-3-classifier.ts while git log --follow returns 22, and every git log -S in this run that is limited to a post-move path therefore reports the move as the introducing commit. That is why 24 of the 28 attributions below can only say pre-v4.0.0.0 and cannot name a date. The fix is one line of durable metadata: a rename map or a documented --follow requirement, since -S and --follow cannot be combined, so a reader has no supported way to answer 'when did this string arrive' across the move.
verify: f=.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/shared/gate-3-classifier.ts; echo plain=$(git log --format=%h -- $f | wc -l) follow=$(git log --follow --format=%h -- $f | wc -l); git ls-tree -r --name-only 330427cf30^ | rg -m2 'gate-3-classifier|cli/spec/validate.sh'

label: CORRECTION to f-iter008-004's release: the silent project-root fallback is not pre-v4. git log -S on the fallback string returns 6f42c7b169, dated 2026-10-31 - after the v4.0.0.16 tag on 2026-10-28 and before v4.0.1.0 on 2026-11-05 - and that commit's own subject is 'fix(system-spec-kit): resolve the project root from the caller's repository'. The regression was therefore introduced by the commit whose stated purpose was to make root resolution caller-relative, which makes it a v4.0.1.0 defect rather than legacy debt and puts it inside the release window this audit covers.
verify: git log --reverse --format='%h %cs %s' -S'not inside a repository that uses spec-kit' -- .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/core/config.ts | head -1

label: Generated outputs are stored under fixtures/ and read back as measurement inputs: generate-trigger-index.mjs:78-80 sets DEFAULT_MANIFEST_PATH, DEFAULT_DIAGNOSTICS_PATH and DEFAULT_VARIANTS_PATH to files inside runtime/cli/retrieval/fixtures, its own header at :35-36 says --out writes all three beside the index, and measure-cold-lookup.mjs:40 then reads that same manifest as the corpus it prices a cold lookuper against. One path serves as generator output and as a fixture, which is why v4.0.0.12's four-file delta is indistinguishable from a rebase. Nothing breaks if the three move under runtime/data beside trigger-index.json: the only readers are the generator defaults and the cold-lookup measurer, and both resolve through exported constants.

note: tag short SHAs recorded in deep-research-config.json are tag-object SHAs, not commits: git rev-parse v4.0.0.0 gives 6e11d39b26 while the prompt's map says 3fed08373e, which git for-each-ref confirms as the *objectname target. v4.0.2.0 is a lightweight tag on 51f70a0317, so the two conventions coexist in one tag series and a reader who mixes them diffs the wrong pair.
